unread_files_or_limits: I read the full tei:text/standOff of all 96 changed documents, but only from the bundles. I did not open the originals, so I have not reviewed the omitted publication/credit/licence header boilerplate.

Files outside the bundles that the changed modules transclude or depend on were not read: the main-service musaf invitation context, kohanim_response_1_1/2_1/2_4/3_1/3_5/3_6, the EN regalim/musaf/text/veteerav and sheotekha providers, the numbers/14/17 provider, morning_full_kaddish.

Not read: existing-identity-corpus-search.json, legacy-identity-evidence.json, draft-kohanim-callers.json, the sequence-review spines, features.yaml and the refdb/compiler code. For note lookup and pre-range declare behaviour I relied on specs/COMPILER_SPECIFICATION.md.
Read-only review. I ran no validation, validate_names, validate_features or compile.

required_changes.issue: BLOCKER. The same citation note appears twice. psalm_92.xml has a standOff citation note with target bible:psalms/92/1 and text 'צב', and daily_psalm_92.xml has an identical one. The same is true for 93/1 ('צג') in psalm_93.xml and daily_psalm_93.xml.
required_changes.evidence: COMPILER_SPECIFICATION.md 'Annotation Processing' says standoff notes are looked up by target URN across the annotation project. 'Print-once annotations' says citation notes are set at every occurrence. JLPTEI-3.md:960 says a note 'is set wherever its target's text is'. So both notes resolve wherever 92:1 or 93:1 is compiled, which gives a doubled citation at least at the p.11 opening. The daily caller's note cannot be confined to the daily context, because its target text is not in that file.
required_changes.remedy: Keep one note per target, in the provider, and delete the standOff from daily_psalm_92 and daily_psalm_93. If the p.11 printing has no citation, add a j:condition to that single note keyed to the daily-appendix wording feature that daily_psalm_* already declares, so it is set only there. Then check one citation per occurrence in compiled output. If compiled output already shows a single citation, downgrade this item.

required_changes.issue: Guideline conformance; rendered output does not change. These speaker and manner rubrics are encoded as tei:note type="instruction". The guideline classifies a rubric that says who says the passage, or how, as a description.
required_changes.evidence: JLPTEI-3.md:2003-2008: 'A description says what the passage printed after it is, who says it, or how: … "Reader:"… It is a tei:note type="description" placed first inside the passage's scope.' Placing them in the context files is correct. Only the type is wrong. The prior review accepted 'instruction' without citing this section.
required_changes.remedy: Change these to type="description" and keep them in the context files. Keep type="instruction" for the directive in musaf_kohanim_yehi_ratzon.xml ('ויכוין לסיים…') and for the conditional rubrics (לכהנים/להעם, בר״ה ויו״כ, בר״ה וי״כ).

notes: Canonical reuse holds up overall. Retzeh, Modim (both fragments), Modim de-rabbanan, ve-al kullam, u-khetov, ve-khol ha-chayyim, Sim shalom, be-sefer, asher qiddeshanu and Addir ba-marom each have one provider per language, with a tei:choice of earlier and kohanim_appendix printings. Each appendix caller declares every printing_N feature of its group. The literal contexts (rh_hodaah, amidah_modim_derabbanan) keep seg/@source copies without corresp, so they do not compete as providers. The s348 page break and the 857 sic/corr sit only inside the appendix options.

The split of response 3_1 is justified. The appendix makes Proverbs 3:4 optional (parenthesised), so the compound legacy part cannot be reused as it stands. Using bible:psalms/24/5 (an option in the Psalm 24 provider) plus an optional, type="marked" bible:proverbs/3/4 avoids a second Hebrew copy of 24:5. The main service keeps its compound legacy part unchanged. The English split files are exact substrings of the p.146 text. 24:5 is left without final punctuation, which is correct for a copy and is not a defect.

Response 2_5 / Psalm 123:2 is valid as encoded but is the weakest reuse decision. The stated reason, keeping out the source-only repeat cue, is already met: the prayer-part terminator before the navigation milestone in musaf_kohanim_response_2_5.xml closes the response scope. Responses 2_2, 2_3, 3_2, 3_3 and 3_4 use a kohanim_appendix option inside the legacy response part. Doing the same for 2_5 would remove kohanim_psalms_123_2_words/translation, and with them the second identical English copy. This is optional.

Preparation: the person.kohen true/false branches share a common opening and ending, and their לכהנים/להעם rubrics are j:conditional instruction notes, as JLPTEI-3.md:1989 requires. The wife/children and parents clauses are independent, type="marked", in both printings. Umetza is optional only in the appendix. The Kaddish al Yisrael additions are independent and marked. Kaddish yatom has no Ten Days guard. The u-khetov and be-sefer high-holidays guards each hold both the rubric and the transclusion.

Biblical quotations: the full chapters use canonical chapter and verse corresps, and the six shared verses (81/4, 81/5, 81/11, 94/1, 94/2, 94/14) are transcluded, not duplicated. The partial Job 20:15 quotation uses quote-context URNs inside seg type="quotation", following JLPTEI-3.md:217-227. Optional: yehi_ratzon_shekol_tippah gives Isaiah 63:9b a canonical half-verse corresp but uses quote-context for the full Deuteronomy 30:3–4 verses. Make these consistent, set seg/@source to isaiah/63/9/b, and fold the two Deuteronomy 30 segs together (dropping the 'second' path segment).

Optional: the j:declare in psalm_94.xml and psalm_81.xml comes before the chapter milestone. It still takes effect, because the external processor RECURSEs through what precedes a range to evaluate declares (COMPILER_SPECIFICATION.md:83-87). But the place rule and the daily_psalm_92/93/24 pattern suggest moving it into daily_psalm_94/81 caller wrappers.

Optional: musaf_kohanim_response_2_5.xml HE still has the dream_repeat navigation milestone and the רבש״ע ref inside a div whose corresp is the shared regalim/musaf/text identity. The reusable priest and response parts are clean, but a caller of the whole div gets the RH cue. Consider moving the cue to the musaf repetition context.
Optional: the two choice options of response_2_5/priest (וִיחֻנֶּֽךָּ) appear identical. Check the bytes, and if they match, drop the vacuous choice together with its declared features.

Optional naming and title fixes: the EN files kohanim_veteerav and kohanim_sheotekha carry Hebrew main titles. 'psalms 24 5' and 'proverbs 3 4' should be 'Psalm 24:5' and 'Proverbs 3:4' (AGENTS.md colon rule). amidah_modim_derabbanan still has the debris title. The file stem kohanim_veteerav and the URN vetearev_lefanekha_atiratenu spell the word differently, so run validate_names. The condition names use five schemes (_earlier, _opening, _printing/earlier, _printing_1/earlier, printing/main); normalise them before promotion.

Optional: several declares set features of the other language (HE vehu_rachum sets marmorstein_translation; EN vehu_rachum and EN rh_avodah set heidenheim printings; closing_kaddish_preface likewise). Harmless now, but noise for strict feature-use checks.

Verify with the spines (out of scope here): the modules have no tei:pb for scans 346, 347, 351, 354 and 355. psalm_24.xml's pb for n350 comes before its chapter milestone, so daily_psalm_24's external bible:psalms/24 transclusion will not emit it. Check that the documentary spine supplies these page markers exactly once.

Accepted as designed: daily_psalm_92/93 transclude inline verse by verse, presumably to avoid copying the p.11 provider's div@facs. This drops verse milestones in the daily context. That is fine for a Hebrew-only documentary appendix, but the expanded-recitation reader should check how it aligns with the English Psalm 92/93.
limitations: Approval is withheld only because of the two module-level required changes (duplicate citation notes; description vs instruction). The third required change concerns registry promotion. Once the first two are fixed, I see no further blocker in the reviewed module encoding.
